clue.text: Politician, dead keen, fighting to banish right wing party

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees
avid means keen or eager

indicators.note: the right wing is taken as the second half of the word, which is removed

parts.note: militant means combative, ready for fighting
a band is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: A politician who is passionately committed, battling to drive out a right-wing faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right wing' is not Conservative politics: it means the right-hand half of MILITANT, so 'to banish right wing' leaves MILI. David Miliband was a British Labour foreign secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: David Miliband served as British Foreign Secretary and a Labour MP, so he is a statesman in public life.

clue.text: West Indies in batting debacle: virtually useless way to get a result

parts.note: a duck is a batsman's score of nothing in cricket, a batting embarrassment

indicators.note: the West Indies abbreviation goes inside the other word
virtually means almost, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: useless means worthless
WI is the standard abbreviation for the West Indies cricket team

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the West Indies batting collapse was hopeless, and rain left a method needed to settle the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUCKWORTH-LEWIS method sets revised targets in rain-shortened one-day cricket matches. 'virtually' drops the last letter of the synonym for useless, and 'in' places the West Indies abbreviation just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket rule for calculating targets in interrupted limited-overs games is a method of reaching an outcome.

clue.text: Swinging sex getting less than top marks

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, written as the Roman numeral VI
a B rating is a grade below the top A

explanation.surface: Wife-swapping pursuits are judged as not quite first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six, so it gives the Roman numeral VI, not anything risque; 'Swinging' looks like part of that scene but is the definition, meaning oscillating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swinging to and fro is oscillating, moving rapidly back and forth.

clue.text: Character in strip club regularly tried exotic clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the anagrammed letters enclose the other piece
exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of tried are rearranged
regularly picks every other letter of club, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A strip club's dancers tried out exotic costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' gives DIERT, which 'clothing' wraps around the letters 'regularly' picks. 'strip' means a comic strip, not stripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilbert is the office-worker hero of Scott Adams's comic strip, so he is a cartoon character.

clue.text: Cousins effectively keep apart from relations

indicators.note: the two words keep the answer inside them, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: A family saying that cousins are, in effect, kept at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: IN SE is Latin for 'in itself', considered intrinsically rather than in relation to anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes something taken by itself, without reference to its connections with other things.

clue.text: Welshman meeting Scots and African statesmen

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name
Ian is the Scottish form of John, so Scotsmen can be Ians

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician meets Scottish ones and some African leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'statesmen' as 'state's men': people of an African state, the Ivory Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Côte d'Ivoire, a West African country, are the men of that state.

clue.text: Fury, perhaps, when cult TV show finishes early

indicators.note: the title is stopped one letter short of its end

parts.note: The Avengers was a cult British spy series of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Anger runs high when a much-loved television programme is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: THE AVENGERS was a stylish 1960s British TV spy series; drop its last letter. 'Fury' with its capital is one of the Furies, mythical avengers, not rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth were spirits of vengeance, so one of them is an example of a punisher seeking retribution.

clue.text: Ruin suit

definitions.meaning: to destroy or wreck someone or something
to be adequate or serve, as in 'that will serve for now'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to finish off or destroy and to be good enough for a purpose.

clue.text: In place of secret messages, very permissive chap takes miss out

parts.note: dead means very, as in dead easy
one who lets, permitting things
to drop is to omit or leave out

explanation.surface: An extremely lax man skips the young woman he was due to take out.
explanation.walkthrough: A dead-letter drop is a hiding place where spies leave messages to be collected without meeting. 'miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb, omit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies use a concealed spot to pass documents without meeting, so it is a hiding place for covert communications.

clue.text: On mend at last, set on running a small part of the way

definitions.text: a small part of the way

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters come at the end, after the other piece

parts.note: to cobble is to mend shoes

indicators.note: running suggests the letters run loose and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to a shoe repairer to finish the job and get the thing going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On mend' could suggest a patient's recovery, but 'mend' is the shoe repairer's verb; 'running' rearranges the two words and 'at last' puts them at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded paving stone is one small piece of an old road surface, so a little bit of the street.

clue.text: Recalled huge, offensive, boxing opponent

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run in reverse
boxing means enclosing, so the words hold the answer inside them across the join

explanation.surface: A boxing commentator remembers a huge, aggressive opponent in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' finds EOF in 'hugE OFfensive', and 'Recalled' turns it round. 'boxing' looks like the sport but is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy or adversary is someone ranged against you.

clue.text: Hunter, comparatively fit, put on weight

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the comparative follows the abbreviation

parts.note: haler is the comparative of hale, meaning healthy

explanation.surface: A hunter, healthier than most, has gained some pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on weight' reads as getting fatter, but it places HALER after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler is a person or ship that hunts whales.

clue.text: Ready to drop grand Hollywood actor into jihad for a bit of a laugh

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the new letters replace the laughing sound within jihad

parts.note: ha is a single burst of laughter
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
Richard Gere is a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: An exhausted Hollywood star is pitched into a holy war just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop ... into ... for' tells you to put G and GERE into JIHAD in place of HA. JIGGERED is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready to collapse means utterly worn out, which the British slang word describes.

clue.text: Is sort to crash parties

indicators.note: crash suggests a collision that scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that this is the type of person who gatecrashes gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges IS SORT. 'parties' is a verb here: to roist is an old word meaning to revel.
explanation.definitionFit: To roist is an archaic verb for revelling noisily, so it means to celebrate or have a good time.

clue.text: Log with iron point causing damage to contestants

parts.note: an entry is an item recorded in a log
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A log fitted with an iron spike injures those competing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is the informal sense of cost, as in 'what's the damage?', not harm.
explanation.definitionFit: What it costs to take part in a competition is the price charged to entrants.

clue.text: German food types avoided by weightwatchers?

parts.note: dieters steer clear of food cooked in fat
dieters also avoid heavy, calorie-laden dishes

explanation.surface: A question about which German dishes slimmers shun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is not a cuisine but a man: Friedrich is a common German first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical German man's name, as borne by Nietzsche, can stand for a German person.

clue.text: We make records: here's one of our hits!

definitions.text: We make records: here's one of our hits!

parts.words: We make records: here's one of our hits!
parts.note: a pop group speaks of its chart records, and 'here's one of our hits' is also what you say while landing a punch

explanation.walkthrough: The British boy band's name is also the exclamation made when striking someone, so 'hits' works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous British boy band of the 1990s had many chart successes, and the phrase is also a cry accompanying a blow.

clue.text: Barrel takes up all space in van

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's share, monopolising room
the van is the front or vanguard, the head

explanation.surface: A big cask fills the whole of the delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is not a vehicle but the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, a kind of barrel holding beer or wine.

clue.text: Help youth to gain such experience?

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A parent's helping their boy gain work experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the kind of experience a son gets by being helped: practical, direct involvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical, direct involvement in a task is described as experience gained by doing.

clue.text: Peer is contemptible person protecting name

indicators.note: protecting means enclosing, so the abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: squit is British slang for a small, insignificant person

explanation.surface: A lord who is a despicable figure is shielding his reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord but is the verb, to look closely; SQUIT is British slang for a contemptible little person.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look narrowly through half-closed eyes, which is what screwing one's eyes up does.

clue.text: Point has run out team's opener: 16 for one

indicators.note: out means one letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a quarter is a point of the compass
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of the word team's

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman is run out and the team's opening player is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R from QUARTER to give QUARTE, then add T. '16' refers to the 16-down solution, the pop group that performed as four.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy band of the other entry was for years a four-piece, so it is an example of a group of four musicians.

clue.text: Bear bringing tongue closer

parts.note: ENG is short for English, a tongue or language
an ender is something that finishes or closes

explanation.surface: A bear is pictured reaching its tongue nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb, to produce or give rise to, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear fruit or results is to produce or bring about, which is to cause something to exist.

clue.text: Feminist would be one concurring with article

indicators.note: the answer with an added article would make the other word, so that article is taken away

parts.note: an agreer is someone who agrees
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A feminist would be someone who agrees with the piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist author. Put the article A in front of her name and it becomes AGREER.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer wrote The Female Eunuch and is a leading campaigner for women's rights.

clue.text: Swede cut by good butcher's

indicators.note: by means beside, so the abbreviation sits next to the shortened name
cut means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Anders is a typical Swedish man's name

explanation.surface: A turnip is chopped up by a skilled meat seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' is a Swedish man, ANDERS, not the vegetable. 'butcher's' is cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, as does GANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Butcher's hook rhymes with look, and a gander is also a glance, so both mean a quick look.

clue.text: Tips from lovely Pamela Stephenson — Big Yin's partner

indicators.note: tips are the ends, here the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Lovely Pamela Stephenson is the wife of Billy Connolly, the comedian nicknamed the Big Yin.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Connolly, the Scottish comedian, is known as the Big Yin and is married to Pamela Stephenson; but the definition is the Chinese principle that pairs with yin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy the active, masculine principle is paired with the passive one, the two complementing each other.

clue.text: Time to finish off Caesar salad starter lacking fish

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the word salad

explanation.surface: A chef says it is time to finish the Caesar salad, minus the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish off Caesar' means kill him, on the Ides of March, not complete the salad; 'lacking' removes S, the starter of 'salad'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Zilch gets fixed with master becoming more sloppy

indicators.note: being fixed suggests the letters are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: A nothing score is repaired with a skilled craftsman's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets fixed' rearranges ZILCH and MASTER together. 'sloppy' means sentimental here.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, and sloppy can mean mawkish, so this is the comparative of sentimental.

clue.text: Effectively manage to ladder a pair of leggings with it

parts.note: a ladder in stockings is a run
tights are a garment worn on the legs
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to snag a pair of trendy tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' is the British word for a run in tights, used here as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical idiom means to keep a well-ordered, disciplined organisation, so to manage it well.
